summary.text: Rachel May is a Democratic state senator who represents New York State Senate District 48 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
May, a former professor and university administrator, has been a state senator since 2019 and is the Democratic and Working Families Party candidate.

paragraphs.text: Rachel May lives in Syracuse, New York.

She earned a B.A. in Slavic languages from Princeton University in 1978, an M.Litt. in modern languages from the University of Oxford in 1981, a Ph.D. in Slavic languages from Stanford University in 1990, and an M.P.S. in environmental science from the State University of New York in 2003.
Her career experience includes working as an associate professor of Russian at Macalester College and as director of the office of environment and society at Syracuse University.
May has served in the State Senate since 2019.

In the 2025-2026 session she chairs the Consumer Protection Committee and is also assigned to the Energy and Telecommunications; Housing, Construction and Community Development; Cities 2; Environmental Conservation; Higher Education; and Investigations and Government Operations committees.
In the November 3, 2026 general election, May faces Richard McCarron (R / Conservative Party).
